growth_signal.value: Two iDEX defence contracts; first six-satellite constellation being built

raised.value: $8M seed in September 2026 led by Blue Ashva Capital, co-led by Finvolve; its first outside funding

entry.idea: Builds small satellites that fly as a swarm, talk to each other and decide together what to look at, so a defence customer gets intelligence in minutes instead of months.
entry.lesson: Win the government contract first and let it fund the hardware; the investors come after the product exists.
entry.name: Kepler Aerospace

growth.basis: substitute: defence contracts and first funding
growth.reason: No revenue numbers; the satellites are not in orbit yet.

market.reason: Governments worldwide are buying surveillance satellites, but the customers are few and the sales cycles long.

tech.reason: Own avionics and a swarm that coordinates itself in orbit; hardware plus autonomy that takes years to build.

entry.twist: It makes the satellite parts itself, the on-board computers, power and radio, and bootstrapped for eight years on Indian defence contracts before taking any outside money.
entry.who_pays: The Indian defence ministry through iDEX contracts, and later other governments and companies needing surveillance data.
entry.why_now: India is pushing private space and defence companies hard, and cheap launches make a six-satellite swarm affordable.

mentions.snippet: Indian space startup building intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance satellites; $8M raised.

Bengaluru; founded 2018 by Navneet Singh and Kiran V Sharma; builds satellite avionics and subsystems; first constellation of six autonomous swarming ISR satellites with optical, thermal and electronic-warfare sensors under two iDEX defence contracts; first outside funding, co-led by Finvolve
